params.message:
A verdict that rested on the wrong evidence can be withdrawn, visibly

The judge refuted two claims against a measurement taken before the change
had landed (elixir#199 stops that happening again). Those two verdicts are
still in the ledger, and a refutation is permanent in the rung: ten
confirmed, zero refuted. One wrong one closes a door that does not reopen.

So a withdrawal, and not a rewrite. The verdict that was passed stays on
the run as wasVerdict with its evidence and the reason it was withdrawn;
the run returns to unjudged and the next reading decides it properly. A
reader sees what happened, the counting sees a run nobody judged yet.

Only a person runs it, and only with a reason: an error that disappears
teaches nobody, and a record that quietly improves is not a record.
